ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The incorporation agent must continuously screen all shareholders with 25% or more direct/indirect ownership, every manager, director, officer, power-of-attorney holder and signatory, and their immediate family members and known close associates against: the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) watch-lists; sanctions imposed by the United Nations Security Council and implemented by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the U.S. OFAC SDN and consolidated lists if any USD clearing, correspondent account, or U.S. payment rail is used; the EU/UK consolidated lists for any European nexus; and the domestic PEP database maintained by financial institutions in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12 and FSC regulations. Screening must be automated and refreshed within 24 hours of a sanctions-list update, with negative-hit escalation to the KoFIU-designated compliance officer and a written SAR/Vulnerability memo retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iros.go.kr) and the competent district court commercial registry for the proposed head office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name of a Yuhan Hoesa must contain the mandatory suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' (limited company) in Korean script. A distinctive Hangul element is normally required; a foreign name may be transliterated into Hangul, and the registration officer must confirm the transliteration is not misleading. The four-tier naming sequence is: (1) distinctive trademark/brand element; (2) descriptive industry element such as 'Hotpot' or 'Dining'; (3) optional geographic element such as 'Seoul'; and (4) the legal suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'. The name must be clearly distinguishable from existing registered names in the same registry district and must not indicate a prohibited business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registration officer refuses a proposed trade name, the applicant may file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act to the district court that issued the refusal, within one week of receiving notice. The written appeal must cite the Commercial Act and demonstrate that the name contains the mandatory limited-company suffix, is not false or misleading, does not invade a protected public symbol, and is not identical or substantially similar to a prior registration in the same registry jurisdiction. The court must rule on documents, and a further immediate appeal to the Supreme Court is available. Concurrently, the applicant should reserve and clear a backstop name so the incorporation is not delayed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox will not be accepted by the National Tax Service, the local municipality, or the food-safety licensing authority as the registered head office of a full-service hotpot restaurant. The Food Sanitation Act and Enforcement Decree require a fixed physical place of business with an inspected kitchen, restrooms, dining area, fire and sanitation systems, and a lease or title document. An administrative virtual office may be used only as a supplementary correspondence address, not as the principal place of business for the restaurant license, VAT registration, or corporate tax filing. The actual restaurant premises must be reported as the business place and principal office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk: High, estimated 75-85% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 90 days after opening. Checklist: restaurant is open and sign displayed; kitchen and washroom sanitary conditions; evidence of food-source traceability; fire and gas safety permits; employment contracts, social insurance, and labor postings; POS terminal and daily sales records; VAT invoices/tax invoices; condiment inventory and storage; business registration certificate posted; lease contract; food waste disposal contract; and manager identification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 4472, as amended), Articles 287-1 through 287-74, governing Yuhan Hoesa limited liability companies; supplemented by the Commercial Registration Rules enacted by the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, administered by the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application, submitted together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act; no statutory minimum paid-in capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa. The amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully deposited into a blocked escrow account in a licensed Korean bank before registration, and a capital deposit certificate issued by that bank must be attached to the incorporation application.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 2025-01 ADOPTED BY WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE INCORPORATORS AND INITIAL EXECUTIVE OFFICERS OF [COMPANY NAME], A YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) (THE 'COMPANY'). WHEREAS, the Company is being organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea as a Yuhan Hoesa with limited liability; and WHEREAS, the Company intends to operate a direct-operated hotpot restaurant and condiment supply business in the Republic of Korea; and WHEREAS, the undersigned incorporators constitute all of the initial members and have appointed themselves as the initial executive officers; NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED: 1. Capital Subscription. The paid-in capital of the Company set forth in the Articles of Incorporation is ratified, and the subscription by each initial member is accepted. The executive officers are instructed to procure the statutory capital deposit certificate from a Korean licensed bank by depositing the full amount into a blocked escrow account, which certificate shall be filed with the incorporation registration package. 2. Banking Authorization. The Company shall open and maintain corporate transactional, foreign exchange, and merchant acquiring accounts with a licensed Korean bank. The representative executive officer and the chief financial officer, if separately appointed, are jointly and severally authorized to execute signature cards, electronic banking instructions, merchant agreements, and all ancillary documents. Any two authorized signatories may act for the Company in banking matters. 3. Registered Office. The registered corporate office is hereby designated as [Address], and the district court of that jurisdiction is selected for commercial registration. The executive officers are directed to execute or procure a lease for such premises and to adjust all construction to comply with building, sanitary, and fire-safety laws. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The incorporators appoint [Name] as representative executive officer and [Name] as finance executive officer, each to serve until successors are elected. The officers, individually or jointly, are authorized to represent the Company before the tax office, fire department, local municipal authorities, and any licensing board in connection with the formulation, placement, and renewal of the Company's licenses and permits. 5. Certification and Filing. The executive officers are directed to execute all regulatory applications, acknowledgements, and undertakings, to pay all registration taxes and fees, and to cause the incorporation registration to be completed prior to the commencement of business. This resolution shall be binding upon all members and their successors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction, assisted by a licensed Korean notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed Korean company name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing corporate names using the commercial registration name search portal of the Supreme Court of Korea. Prepare notarized Articles of Incorporation in Korean, with an English translation for governance convenience, ensuring the Korean text prevails for registration. The content must include the company name, registered office address, precise corporate purpose covering hotpot dining and condiment supply, capital contribution schedule, initial members, executive officer limitation clauses, and public notice method. Each incorporator must execute the articles in person in front of a notary, or by counsel with lawful power of attorney. Once notarized, the articles become the constitutional charter for subsequent filings, and the original certified duplicate is the main exhibit for the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of every initial member
Evidence of registered address in Korea if resident
Power of attorney if executed by proxy
Consent of all initial executive officers
Name availability search result from the registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the company name or articles, correct the name or supplementary clauses and obtain a newly notarized version within seven days; request an administrative correction under the Commercial Registration Rules, or appeal to the relevant court for a formal objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed Korean commercial bank authorized to issue corporate accounts and capital deposit certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a pre-registration corporate escrow account in the entity denomination, deposit the full amount of paid-in capital referred to in the Articles of Incorporation, and obtain the statutory capital deposit certificate issued by the bank manager. The account remains sealed until the court confirms registration. For non-resident members, the foreign exchange remittance must be reported to the bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act when applicable, and all source-of-funds information must comply with anti-money-laundering verification standards. The capital deposit certificate must be dated no earlier than registration day and must name the planned Yuhan Hoesa as the beneficiary.
required_dossiers: Foreign capital remittance receipt if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds issuance due to anti-money-laundering queries, provide source-of-funds documentation and an executed beneficial ownership declaration; repeat the deposit after KYC clearance, or select another licensed Korean bank and issue a replacement certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court at the registered office jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application through the online court registration portal or in person, attaching the statutory instruments including the notarized Articles, capital deposit certificate, written consent or membership subscription statement of initial members, executive officer appointment acceptance letters, and certified copy of the first board resolution. Pay the registration tax and the court fee by electronic transfer. After examiners verify that the documents comply with Articles 287-1 to 287-74 of the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Rules, the company receives its company registration number and a corporate certificate of registration. The process must be completed before any business activity begins.
required_dossiers: Executed lease or title document for the corporate registered address
Power of attorney to the registration agent
Proof of payment of registration tax and fee
Signature specimen of the representative executive officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner issues a formal deficiency notice, rectify the missing certificate no later than ten days; if the application is rejected, prepare and file a new application with supplementary reasons within fourteen days; appeal to the district court panel if the refusal appears legally invalid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Taxpayer Identification with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the newly issued corporate registration certificate, file an application for business registration under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act and Article 168 of the Income Tax Act within twenty days from incorporation. The application may be made through the HomeTax portal or in person at the district tax office. Register the corporate business code, invoice issuance mechanism, and intended taxable operations, and obtain the Business Registration Certificate together with the corporate taxpayer identification number. The same process registers the entity for corporate tax, value-added tax, and employee withholding obligations.
required_dossiers: Identification of the representative executive officer
Application form for general business registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office identifies a mismatch in company name or address, file a supervening correction through HomeTax or in person with the original registration documents; if the tax office requires additional attendance or documents, provide the requested items and obtain the certificate after rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Restaurant Operating License and Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal government (Si/Gun/Gu Office) Food Sanitation Department and the local Fire Station under the National Fire Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must initiate the food business license application before physical opening under the Food Sanitation Act. Submit the license form with the layout drawings, kitchen ventilation specifications, sanitation plan, and fire safety documents. The local hygiene inspector and fire safety officer jointly conduct an on-site inspection of the kitchen ventilation, gas installations, sewage connection, and fire equipment. After passing, the local government issues the General Restaurant Food Business License, while the fire department issues the Fire Facility Completion Certificate. This process must follow building code approval and safety inspection.
required_dossiers: Restaurant floor plan drawn to scale
Food sanitation course certificate of the responsible manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license is suspended or refused due to facility defects, cure the specific deficiencies and apply for a re-inspection using the same application reference number within ten business days; if the refusal persists, file an administrative appeal with the competent mayor or governor and exhaust the Administrative Litigation Act remedies if necessary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Municipal Food Sanitation Division (Si/Gun/Gu) and the Fire Station under the National Fire Agency, supervised by the Ministry of Environment for discharge matters
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Restaurant Food Business License (Eating-Place Operating Permit) under the Food Sanitation Act, together with Fire Facility Completion Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and the local consultative Environmental Authority (Environmental Management Office)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report; classified as a low-impact category requiring only environmental registration and discharge compliance for a non-manufacturing restaurant under the Water Quality Conservation Act and the air quality regulations for kitchen exhaust
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Kitchen wastewater must meet the following effluent standards before entering the public sewer: pH 5.8-8.6, BOD 80 mg/L maximum, COD 80 mg/L maximum, suspended solids 80 mg/L maximum, and oil/grease 50 mg/L maximum. Cooking fumes must pass through a grease filter and an exhaust hood with PM removal efficiency of at least 85% and an exhaust flow rate of 300 CFM or higher per range. Hazardous waste such as used cooking oil must be delivered to licensed collectors under the Waste Management Act and must never enter the drain.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Inspection and Facility Completion Certificate must be procured from the local fire authority, covering emergency lighting, exit signs, extinguishers, gas safety valve, automatic gas leak detection, and, if required, an automatic sprinkler system in the kitchen or dining area. Additionally, the municipal building authority must issue certification of general construction safety and electrical wiring approval. The employer must post occupational hygiene notices, conduct basic fire safety education, carry out workplace pollution health checks where relevant, and subscribe employees to industrial accident compensation insurance for the restaurant operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: HomeTax electronic tax filing system (https://www.hometax.go.kr/); customs administration: Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic customs clearance system (https://unipass.customs.go.kr/)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The operating entity is a Korean Yuhan Hoesa (domestic corporation) and must obtain a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) from the NTS, which serves as both the corporate TIN and VAT registration number. The entity must submit a business operator registration application with the head of the district tax office having jurisdiction over the actual domestic place of business within 20 days of business commencement, under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act and Article 168 of the Corporate Tax Act. A foreign non-resident shareholder is not required to be physically present in Korea; the Yuhan Hoesa itself is the taxable person. If the foreign parent or a non-resident entity without a domestic place of business directly performs VAT-taxable supplies in Korea, it must appoint a domestic tax representative under Article 22 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and file the prescribed business registration application through the tax representative. Supporting documents for registration include: articles of incorporation and incorporation certificate (apostilled/consular-legalized as required), power of attorney for the tax representative or resident director, lease or ownership documents proving the Korean place of business, foreign investment report certificate under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if a foreign investment report has been made, and identification/tax residence evidence for the representative. The NTS issues a Business Registration Certificate and assigns the BRN; registration is effective from the date of business commencement. The Korean Yuhan Hoesa is classified as a domestic corporation, so it is not eligible for individual simple-taxpayer registration and is mandatorily a general VAT taxable person.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa. The entity is per se treated as a domestic corporation for Corporate Tax Act, Value-Added Tax Act, and international tax treaty purposes, and no hybrid mismatch entity election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax Act; national Korean VAT administered by the NTS; no separate sub-national sales tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 for an incorporated Yuhan Hoesa. There is no turnover exemption for a corporation; registration as a general taxable person is mandatory from day one of business commencement. The simplified taxable person threshold of KRW 80,000,000 for individual businesses is not available to this entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A general taxable person must issue a VAT invoice for taxable supplies of goods and services. Electronic tax invoicing (e-tax invoice) is mandatory for all general taxable persons. The e-tax invoice must be issued through the NTS HomeTax electronic tax invoice system or through an integrated ERP/API connection that transmits the invoice data to HomeTax. The NTS validates the electronic serial number and uses real-time data matching across the issuer, recipient, customs, and payment systems as an anti-fraud control; there is no physical tax stamp or prepayment fiscal clearance device. For B2C restaurant and retail condiment sales, a VAT invoice must be issued when requested by the customer, and cash receipts must be issued through the approved cash-receipt system for cash transactions; credit card transaction data is automatically transmitted to the NTS by the payment acquirer. E-tax invoice data for supplies between businesses must be transmitted to the NTS by the statutory deadline prescribed in Article 32 of the Value-Added Tax Act, and inaccurate or late transmission exposes the entity to additional tax penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act where goods are exported from Korea and the export declaration is accepted by Korea Customs Service; title, risk, and physical possession must pass to the foreign buyer and the goods must leave the Korean customs territory. For qualifying exported services, zero-rating applies when the service is supplied to a non-resident, the recipient of the service is located outside Korea, the effective use and enjoyment of the service occurs outside Korea, and the service is classified as a service export eligible for zero-rating under the Value-Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree. Dining services rendered by a Korean restaurant to customers inside Korea are standard-rated at 10% and cannot be zero-rated merely because the customer is a foreign tourist. Condiment products delivered to overseas related restaurants or distributors can be zero-rated as exported goods only if accompanied by a valid customs export declaration and related evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Acceptance Certificate issued by Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS system)
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Purchase Confirmation issued by a licensed foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Sales contract or purchase order with the foreign buyer
Certificate of Origin if required for customs clearance or FTA preference
Performance certificate or signed delivery receipt evidencing overseas receipt of the goods or services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is scrutinized by matching the NTS VAT return, Korea Customs Service export declaration data, bank foreign exchange receipts, and the e-tax invoices issued. If the export declaration is absent, void, or corrected to domestic supply, if the Inward Remittance Certificate is not in the name of the Korean exporter, if export proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days without a valid extension granted by the foreign exchange bank, or if the service export cannot reasonably prove that the recipient is non-resident and the place of use is outside Korea, the NTS will reverse the zero-rating and assess VAT at the standard 10% rate on the supply value. In addition, statutory additional taxes under the Value-Added Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes are imposed, including penalties for false or unfaithful e-tax invoices and underdeclared tax. Fraudulent or intentionally false export claims exposes the entity and its responsible officers to aggravated tax penalties and criminal prosecution under the Punishment for Tax Offenses Act. The ordinary statute of limitations for VAT assessment is five years, extended to ten years where the underreporting is deliberate and concealed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting as the central monetary and foreign exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with policy coordination by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and operational reporting through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) administered by the Bank of Korea and delegated foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is deemed convertible for current-account items such as trade settlements, royalties, dividends, service payments, and operational branch transfers, provided the submitting entity can evidence the underlying transaction with commercial documents and the designated foreign exchange bank validates the filing. Capital-account items, including equity injections, cross-border loans, securities investments, guarantees, and related financial transfers, are conditionally convertible: they are permitted only with prior or simultaneous notification to the Bank of Korea or the delegated foreign exchange bank and are subject to post-transaction documentary audit. There is no mandatory ratio for forcibly converting export proceeds into KRW, but export earnings must be received through a licensed bank and reported with a valid export declaration and a matching collection settlement. Profit remittance from a Korean Yuhan Hoesa is lawful only after corporate income taxes and dividend withholding taxes are settled, the annual external audit is available, and the remittance classification is recorded in the Foreign Exchange Information System. Banks will require the entity's business registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, board or shareholder resolutions, audited financial statements, and the foreign exchange bank agreement before executing any capital or dividend outflow. In practice, the system is a highly documented, proportionate control regime: it neither prohibits convertibility nor permits unrestricted free-floating access; it instead disciplines all cross-border flows through banking intermediation, transaction coding, and BOK oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Korean foreign exchange regulations, exporters must repatriate and settle export proceeds within six (6) months from the date of export declaration, unless an extension is approved by the designated foreign exchange bank for valid commercial reasons such as deferred payment terms. There is no statutory percentage requiring conversion of export earnings into KRW; the proportion held in foreign currency may remain in a foreign currency account, but the full amount must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Information System and supported by the customs export declaration, commercial invoice, and bank collection confirmation. For a hotpot chain also supplying condiments overseas, every shipment requires a matching customs export declaration and bank receipt to evidence bona fide trade, and any excess delay beyond the six-month window must be justified to the foreign exchange bank to avoid administrative penalties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Global fintech EMIs, digital wallets, and non-bank payment institutions are generally not viable as the primary treasury or clearing rail for a Korean-resident Yuhan Hoesa. Korea's Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act require licensed domestic foreign exchange banks to execute cross-border remittances, maintain KRW clearing accounts, and file Foreign Exchange Information System reports. Non-bank EMIs cannot lawfully maintain a full corporate multi-currency treasury account for a Korean entity, cannot perform capital verification for foreign direct investment, and cannot issue a credible bank confirmation for dividend remittance or export proceeds collection. Such EMIs may only be employed as offshore collection points in the overseas restaurant markets, with automatic settlement into the Korean operating bank, and only after the Korean bank approves the arrangement as part of ancillary payment acceptance. For the core treasury mandate, a licensed domestic Tier-1 bank is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean banks require the statutory directors and authorized signatories to appear physically at a domestic branch for the initial corporate KYC and interview, especially when non-resident directors are present or the entity has a cross-border ownership structure. Remote opening through consular proxy is not generally available; some banks will accept an apostilled power of attorney and a video-based director verification only as a secondary step, but the standard underwriting posture remains that at least one resident director or a designated resident compliance officer must attend an in-branch meeting in person. For a Korean parent company with overseas hotpot restaurants, the compliance team should assign a resident director or a senior treasury officer in Seoul with corporate seal authority to satisfy the in-branch mandate, while overseas directors may be onboarded through notarized passports, apostilled corporate resolutions, and AML questionnaires in parallel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership and opaque ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full ownership map from each natural person shareholder to the Korean Yuhan Hoesa; apostilled incorporation certificates, share ledgers, trust declarations, nominee declarations, source of wealth statements, source of funds bank statements, audited financial statements of the parent entity, and a formal legal opinion from Korean counsel confirming the absence of undisclosed beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags on condiment export invoicing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bone fide trade proof including customs export declarations, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, transport documents, third-party inspection certificates, transfer pricing documentation, intercompany supply contracts, and bank statements showing settlement payments from overseas hotpot restaurants; independent pricing benchmarks for the condiment and seasoning shipments must be retained to counter invoice manipulation allegations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection mismatch and round-tripping exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank of Korea foreign investment notification or pre-screening acknowledgement, board resolutions approving the equity contribution, shareholders register, subscription agreement, audited financial statements of the remitting investor, bank credit facility confirmation from the investor's local bank, and a sworn undertaking that no back-to-back loan or circular funding is being provided by the Korean entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEPs, and adverse media screening on directors and shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled passport copies of every director and ultimate beneficial owner, tax residence certificates, PEP declarations, negative media screening reports from reputable databases, court records and police certificates from countries of residence, CVs and professional references, Korean-language notarized translations of all non-Korean documents, and a signed AML eligibility representation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must be routed through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank via SWIFT wire transfer, with the remittance account name matching the investor's name and the payment narrative clearly identifying the transaction as a capital contribution to a Korean entity. The bank will require the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code for a foreign direct investment capital receipt, the underlying board resolution, the corporate registration documents, and the subscription contract before crediting the funds to the Capital Escrow Account or a foreign currency settlement account. Once the Bank of Korea notification or foreign investment acknowledgement is completed, the funds may be converted to KRW at the onshore market rate and transferred to the operating current account. The company's external auditor must subsequently verify the paid-in capital amount through a capital verification procedure, matching the bank confirmation, the general ledger, the shareholders register, and the BOK notification.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border settlement for the overseas hotpot chain and condiment supply should prioritize SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for direct and trust-based trade payments, Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700/MT720 and related reimbursement) for larger inventory shipments, and Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) only for repeat low-risk customers. All outbound payments must carry the underlying invoice, customs export declaration, transport documentation, and the appropriate Foreign Exchange Information System purpose code. Domestic KRW legs should be settled over BOK-Wire+, the Bank of Korea's high-value interbank settlement rail, while foreign exchange conversion is executed at the dealing bank's onshore market desk. For structural capital flows such as loans, equity returns, or royalty payments, the Korean tax clearance certificate and evidence of settlement through the licensed foreign exchange bank must be attached to the MT103 instruction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts with a licensed Korean bank, supported by a real trade or investment exposure
Currency swap agreements with a licensed bank for long-term operating loans, lease liabilities, or cross-border intercompany funding, provided an underlying exposure exists
Outright FX option purchases for hedging known future export or import cash flows, including premium payment only, without speculative naked option writing

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be considered through global banking channels only for offshore subsidiaries or non-Korean revenue flows, subject to BOK real-demand review, and cannot be used as a speculative substitute for onshore deliverable forwards; pure speculative or unbacked hedging positions are beyond the permissible boundary for a Korean operating entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Return and Local Corporate Income Surtax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, and the competent Local Tax Office for the 10% local corporate income surtax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for an entity with a December 31 year-end, the return must be filed by March 31 of the immediately succeeding year. If the company uses the NTS e-filing system (HomeTax), the deadline is extended by up to 25 business days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Negligence penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax for non-filing or under-declaration; unpaid corporate tax accrues an additional interest charge of 0.022% per day (annualised approximately 8.03%) from the day after the statutory deadline. If the return remains unfiled for six months, the NTS will conduct a deemed assessment, seize bank deposits and trade receivables, and the company may be placed on the 'business not operating' list, ultimately leading to administrative strike-off of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Approval of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal shareholders' meeting under the Korean Commercial Act; if an external audit is mandatory, the audited financial statements must also be filed with the Financial Supervisory Service's DART electronic disclosure system and transmitted to the NTS in the standard XML tax financial statement form.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; for a December fiscal year the meeting must occur by June 30 of the next year. If audit is mandatory, the audited financial statements are transmitted to the NTS concurrently with the corporate tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM or to prepare financial statements without a reasonable cause imposes administrative fines under the Commercial Act of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,800) per violation. Where an external audit is required, absence of the audit report makes the corporate tax return incomplete and may trigger the denial of the tax-loss carryforward and, in cases of repeated violation, the court may issue an order for compulsory dissolution or the registry office may administer a strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Report (Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 31 and 32)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE), processed through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Foreign Investment Support Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the close of each fiscal year (for a December year-end, by January 30 of the following year). The report must state current foreign ownership percentage, total foreign investment amount, number of shares issued, and any subsequent changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An administrative fine not exceeding KRW 10,000,000 (approximately USD 7,600) under Article 36 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-filing, delayed filing, or false reporting. Continuous non-compliance may lead to cancellation of foreign-investment registration and forfeiture of tax incentives; the company may also be barred from future foreign currency remittance and ultimately struck from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation and Anti-Money-Laundering Amendment Filing (Beneficial Ownership Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) of the Financial Services Commission; for cross-border share transactions also the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Korea Customs Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The company must confirm its beneficial ownership information annually by March 31 of the following year for the prior calendar year. Additionally, any transfer of shares, changes to voting rights, or change in beneficial ownership exceeding 1% of total shares must be reported to KoFIU within 30 calendar days of the transfer or change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Wilful or negligent non-disclosure of beneficial ownership information is punishable under the Financial Transaction Reports Act by imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 38,000). Each day of delay is treated as a separate violation for administrative fines; the FIU may also impose a business suspension order, and unresolved AML compliance flags may cause the company's business registration to be suspended.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Tax Payment and Business Registration Status Confirmation (including local corporate income surtax, property tax on business premises, and personal/local occupation tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government / City Hall (for local taxes) and the District Office of the NTS for business registration status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Business registration remains effective without annual re-application; local corporate income surtax is due with the corporate tax return by March 31; property tax in July (for buildings used in restaurant operations) and September for land; each local tax bill is payable within 31 days of issuance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax non-payment triggers a delinquent charge of 3% of the unpaid amount, plus an additional charge of 0.75% for every month of delay; the local authority may issue a compulsory collection order and seize equipment, inventory, and bank accounts. Unpaid local taxes also prevent issuance of a tax clearance certificate, which is indispensable for currency remittances, dissolution, or changing the registered overseas branch chain ownership.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (as amended and delegated to the Korea Institute of Certified Public Accountants), an independent certified CPA audit becomes compulsory if any of the following quantitative thresholds is exceeded at the end of the fiscal year: (a) Balance-sheet total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.2 million); (b) Annual turnover (gross sales) equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.7 million); or (c) The average number of full-time equivalent employees during the fiscal year equals or exceeds 300 persons. Audit is also mandatory when the company is part of a consolidation group where the Korean parent or foreign parent's consolidated total assets exceed these thresholds, when the entity is a financial institution, when the company issues securities to the public, or when the company has been directed to submit an audit report by the Financial Supervisory Service or tax authorities. For companies that do not trigger these thresholds, no statutory independent audit is required; however, the NTS may order a special tax audit or require a CPA review in cases of suspected irregularities or unreported condiment export sales.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The company must prepare its statutory financial statements under either Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS, as published by the Korean Accounting Standards Board) or Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP), with the K-GAAP SME simplified standard available to non-public entities below the audit thresholds. If an external audit is triggered, the engagement must be performed in accordance with the Korean Standards on Auditing (KR-SA) issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At least once each fiscal year, the board of directors must convene, review, and issue an annual beneficial ownership confirmation statement. The confirmation must be adopted at the AGM and must record all direct and indirect beneficial owners holding at least 1% voting rights or equity interest. Any transfer of shares, any change in control of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, or any change of a foreign ultimate beneficial owner must be reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) within 30 calendar days of the underlying transaction. In parallel, the foreign investment report to MOTIE/KOTRA must be updated within 30 days. The statutory register must be physically kept at the registered office in South Korea and must show the date, nature, and notarised evidence of each transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges or Mortgages (Register of Encumbrances)
Minute Book of Directors' and Shareholders' Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - 3,500 annually for a licensed corporate secretarial agent and registered office physical address in Seoul or Busan (includes mail forwarding, annual register maintenance, and government filing coordination)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 - 22,000 for a full statutory audit if any threshold is exceeded, with complexity factors including hotpot restaurant inventory, condiment supply, intercompany transactions and local VAT reporting; for a sub-threshold entity a CPA review or agreed-upon procedures may cost USD 2,500 - 5,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% to 24% progressive corporate income tax (CIT) on taxable income for FY2024 (9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% on the excess between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 21% on the excess between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion; 24% on the excess over KRW 300 billion), plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national CIT, producing an aggregate top marginal rate of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea grants no general statutory tax holiday for restaurant or food-service operations. A Yuhan Hoesa classified as a Small or Medium Enterprise (SME) may reduce computed CIT by 10% to 30% under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, may claim employment and social-insurance tax credits, may claim R&D tax credits on qualifying food-technology development, and may claim a foreign tax credit under Article 57 of the Corporate Tax Act for income tax paid in the overseas jurisdiction where the direct-operated hotpot restaurants and condiment supply activities generate source income. Free-zone and process-zone incentives are generally unavailable to onshore restaurant chains; instead, the practical effective rate is reduced through expense-timing, entertainment-expense truncation and the 15-year loss carryforward rather than through a patent box.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 60 (Separate Form 60) - Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Return (Corporate Income Tax Return of Tax Base and Tax Amount), together with attached financial statements, the tax-adjustment schedule, the related-party international transaction report, and the foreign tax credit worksheet. The return is filed electronically through HomeTax (the National Tax Service e-Tax portal, www.hometax.go.kr) or by registered post to the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the Yuhan Hoesa's place of tax payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, by business year. Domestic corporations must also make two interim prepayments of the preceding year's CIT during the current business year (generally 31 August and 28 February), unless the Yuhan Hoesa qualifies as a newly established SME or has annual tax liability below the statutory de minimis threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate tax return must be filed within 3 months after the close of each fiscal year under Article 60 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. For a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa ending on 31 December, the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year; the deadline may be extended to 30 April when the return is co-signed by an authorised tax agent (certified public accountant or tax accountant), but the extension does not defer the payment of any final tax due without sustaining late-payment interest from the original statutory date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate identification, business registration number, representative, fiscal year and foreign-invested enterprise designation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Yuhan Hoesa, the 10-digit business registration number (saupja deungnok beonho) issued by the Korean District Tax Office, registered office address, representative director name, business year (for example 1 January to 31 December), tax classification code, and the foreign-invested enterprise code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full legal name in Latin characters exactly as registered. Disclose the name, foreign tax-resident country and registered address of each non-resident shareholder in the shareholder schedule. Mark the foreign-invested enterprise checkbox only when a non-resident holds at least 3% of the shares and has filed a foreign-investment report with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (or KOTRA) before the capital contribution; if this status is omitted, the system will apply the statutory 22% withholding rate to any subsequent dividend remittance and no treaty reduction can be claimed retroactively except through a formal refund procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Financial position and profit or loss statement used as the starting point of the tax reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from direct-operated hotpot restaurants, retail sales of hotpot condiments and sauces, franchise and licence income, cost of goods sold, gross profit, selling, general and administrative expenses, operating income, non-operating income, non-operating expenses and pre-tax net income for the business year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise all revenue in KRW on an accrual basis. Include income from all overseas branches of the Yuhan Hoesa in the Korean worldwide taxable base; where an overseas permanent establishment has paid local corporate tax abroad, attach the foreign tax credit worksheet. Intercompany purchases of raw materials, condiments and packaging supplied by foreign related parties must be separately disclosed in the international transaction schedule when the aggregate cross-border related-party transaction amount reaches the statutory reporting threshold; a summary transfer-pricing study reflecting the arm's-length margin of the tested party and a headcount chart of Korean core income-generating activities (CIGA) should accompany the return where a foreign related party is in the distribution chain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Non-deductible expenses and add-back adjustments (disallowed items)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments that increase taxable income: non-deductible entertainment and hospitality expenses exceeding statutory limits, fines and penalties, corporate income tax borne on behalf of shareholders, excessive director remuneration recognised as a constructive dividend, non-statutory reserves, deemed-dividend items on interest-free shareholder loans, and denied interest on debt exceeding the thin-capitalisation ratio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any Korean income tax paid for the benefit of a non-resident shareholder, any expense settlement made to a foreign related party without a written service agreement or cost-contribution arrangement, interest on loans from controlling foreign shareholders for debt in excess of a 3:1 debt-to-equity ratio, and the amortisation of intangible licence fees paid to a foreign shell affiliate unless the price and the beneficial ownership of the licence have been substantiated under the OECD transfer-pricing framework.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Deductible items, statutory reserves, loss carryforwards and exemption adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments that decrease taxable income: statutory bad-debt reserves, inventory valuation adjustments, translation differences, tax-exempt income, special reserves for overseas investment losses where statutory conditions are met, and the off-set of net operating losses carried forward from previous business years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset net operating losses carried forward for up to 15 years from the loss year; a large enterprise may offset only 60% of current-year taxable income with brought-forward losses, while an SME Yuhan Hoesa may offset 100%. Claim foreign taxes as a credit, not as a deduction; overseas withholding taxes on branch profits are creditable only if the treaty and the foreign tax credit schedule are detailed in the return. Do not deduct outbound dividend royalties paid to a foreign parent in the absence of an arm's-length licence determined under Chapter VI of the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax base (taxable income) computation for the non-resident and domestic components
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income equals book pre-tax income plus the add-back adjustments in Box 3 minus the deductions in Box 4, and then reduced by the available net operating loss carryforward, resulting in the corporate income tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file a separate Korean return for dividends; the Yuhan Hoesa computes its worldwide tax base as a domestic corporation. Where the overseas hotpot operations are conducted through a foreign permanent establishment, the profit attributable to the Korean head office must be allocated under the Authorised OECD Approach using functional and factual analysis; a mere book entry shifting profit to the foreign RO without Korean employees performing sourcing and brand management will be re-attributed to Korea under the substance-over-form doctrine.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Computed tax applying the progressive rate schedule and the 10% local income tax surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of national corporate income tax at 9%, 19%, 21% and 24% marginal brackets on the tax base, followed by the separate 10% local income tax surcharge, producing the total computed tax liability before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Box 6 is calculated at the full Korean domestic rates; a bilateral tax treaty does not reduce the Korean rate at the level of the Yuhan Hoesa's return because the treaty concession applies to the foreign shareholder's dividend withholding at remittance. If the entity is a foreign-invested company and has been granted an SME tax reduction, apply the reduction only after the computed national tax, but never reduce the 10% local income tax surcharge in a manner inconsistent with the Local Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Tax credits, tax reductions and interim prepayments (foreign tax credit, SME reduction, R&D credit, prior prepayments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction from the computed tax of the foreign tax credit, the SME tax reduction, the R&D tax credit, the employment tax credit, and the semi-annual interim prepayments made during the current business year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a separate foreign tax credit schedule identifying each foreign jurisdiction, the amount of foreign-source income, the foreign tax paid and the credit limitation computed on a per-country basis. Do not use Box 7 to correct over-withheld Korean dividend tax; treaty refunds are obtained by the non-resident beneficiary through the withholding-office refund procedure. Interim prepayments made by a newly established foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa may be waived where the prior-year tax does not exceed the statutory threshold; otherwise any underpayment of interim tax triggers a 0.022% daily late-payment surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Tax payable after credits, net amount to be paid to the national treasury and final statutory declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final national corporate income tax payable after subtracting all credits and interim prepayments, the amount due to the national treasury, and the computed local income tax surcharge; this box also drives the schedule of non-resident dividend withholding tax and the amount actually remitted abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that any outward remittance of dividends, interest or royalties to a non-resident shareholder was subject to statutory withholding tax of 22% (or the treaty rate where the completed Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership declaration are on file with the withholding office) before the remittance was made. The withholding return for the month of payment must be filed within 10 days after the end of the following month; an unreported remittance exposes the company and the responsible director to a 10% withholding penalty, late-payment interest and criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act. In a year where the Yuhan Hoesa has an overseas hotpot chain but declares a loss while remitting high royalties, the National Tax Service will challenge the economic substance of the intangible payments and recharacterize the profit as Korean-source.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the corporate tax return by the statutory deadline triggers a 20% non-filing penalty on the amount of the payable tax under Article 47-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. A false or fraudulent understatement of income triggers a 40% under-reporting surcharge on the understated tax, while a negligent understatement triggers a 10% surcharge. Unpaid tax carries late-payment interest of 0.022% per day (approximately 3.5% per annum) from the original deadline until the date of payment, and an additional 0.03% daily penalty is assessed where the return is filed after the issuance of a tax reassessment notice. Intentional concealment or fictitious bookkeeping involving an evaded corporate tax amount exceeding KRW 200 million is referred to the public prosecutor under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act and may result in imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to 3 times the tax evaded, with asset seizure, travel prohibition and the blacklisting of the representative director.
